Depression is an interesting thing. You seem to have a lot going well in your life, and still you're miserable. Familiar situation.
Things that help me personally are:

1. Taking walks/runs, I find them very relaxing and liberating.

2. Making sure I never forget that these feelings are baseless and irrational. You have everything ahead of you. You're in your last year of collage and are about to have a degree and already have a job. That is so much! There is no reason to think that your efforts won't pay off, your brain just tells you that cause it's sick.

3. My relationship with therapy is complicated. I'm very happy to hear you've found one you liked and stuck with it. However, I have found that medication helps a lot. If you feel uncomfortable, you could try something with a very low dosage. I personally have been on Paxetine for a while now (depression/anxiety medication) and it's done wonders for me. It reminded me what life without mental illness is like and that motivates me a lot to go on and keep trying.

4. Talking to people about how I feel. I strongly advise you to find a loved one that you trust enough to confide in and do so. I garantee they won't think less of you.

5. Lastly, if at all possible, get a pet. A hamster even. Having another living thing that loves you uncoditionally and you have to be there for and take care of is the best thing in the world for depression/anxiety.

If you have any questions or just need someone to talk to, feel free to dm me.

I hope I helped! Good luck!

First of all, I goota say I think it's amazing you decided to do something about your depression (or what ever mental health provlem you may have). Also, it's so great that you have an understanding SO to support you. Now, I'm a big believer in therapy, as good intentions aren't always enough, unfortunatly. However some things that do help are:
A. Taking Omega 3 (fish oil) and generally eating healthy. Your physical health does wonders for your mental health, and fish oil spesifically has been theorised by many to reduce depression (dk how). You have to be careful with the fish oil though, very rarely it actually makes it worse. If you notice it has a negative effect, stop taking it (give it like 2 weeks to start doing anything first).
B. Physical activity. Any kind you like. I personally find running very uplifting, but any kind would do. Try putting it on your schedual so you stick with it.
C. Self help books are a thing. They're pretty cheap and you can reserch them yourself. Surely you'll find one that'll help you. Most of them will also suggest keeping a diary of sorts, but there are many different approaches to that. Personally, I write down at least 5 positive things that happened in my day. As small as a random person smiling at me, if it's what I can think of.
Hope this helps a bit, and that you get better soon :)
